positions.catalyst: FEED VERIFIED LIVE BEFORE PRICING, TWICE, PER THE FIX I WROTE INTO THE LAST RUN. Proxy pulls at 2026-09-09T10:40:43.963Z, 10:40:57.798Z and 10:40:58.550Z all returned asOf stamps within seconds of wall-clock (10:40:38Z). No repeat of the twelve-day cached response that nearly booked a phantom $96 gain last night. Crypto proved liveness independently: BTC-USD came back 79,102.51 against last night's 78,626.99, i.e. the feed moved overnight rather than replaying a snapshot. Equities correctly show the 9/8 settled close in the proxy because it is 05:40 CT pre-market and Yahoo has not rolled to the pre-market tape; every 9/8 close the proxy returned (UCO 49.35, USO 146.03, SOXL 123.27, SPY 765.96, XLE 64.77) matched Robinhood's sip-list-exchange-close for 9/8 exactly, interpolated=false. So the proxy is right and simply lagging; live pre-market pricing came from Robinhood's real-time book at ~10:41Z. THE SCHEDULER FIRED. First on-time consecutive-day rotation since 8/31 — the multi-session carries that distorted the last two positions did not repeat. THE TRADE WORKED, AND IT WORKED FOR THE STATED REASON, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE P&L. Last night's entire thesis was one measurable claim: UCO's 4pm mark of 49.35 priced WTI at its 93.03 settle while WTI was already trading 94.52, and that gap would transmit when the wrapper reopened. It transmitted. WTI is 94.92 (+2.03% off the settle) and Brent is 100.44 (+2.57%), through $100 FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE JULY. UCO's pre-market last trade is 50.3502 at 10:27:28Z on a 50.34 bid. CLOSED UCO AT 50.34 FOR +$194.39 (+1.74%) IN FIFTEEN HOURS. The gap-capture leg is now realized and, importantly, IS NO LONGER AVAILABLE — that edge is spent and today's decision cannot lean on it. WHY THE CATALYST GOT LARGER OVERNIGHT RATHER THAN SMALLER. Per CNBC, NBC News and Bloomberg: the US struck multiple IRGC-linked tankers and then targets near KHARG ISLAND, the terminal handling up to 90% of Iranian crude exports; Iranian state media reported successive explosions there and at Jask. This follows Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco installations at Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, after which Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry CONFIRMED SUSPENDED OPERATIONS at several oil facilities and utilities. Goldman states that intensifying shipping attacks are raising the probability of Brent above 120. The escalation is tit-for-tat and accelerating; there is no scheduled de-escalation event inside my holding window. TODAY'S PRE-MARKET TAPE (Robinhood real-time, ~10:41Z, vs 9/8 closes). Energy bid across the board: UCO 50.35 (+2.03%), BNO 58.83 (+1.90%), USO 148.23 (+1.51%), XOP 195.98 (+1.07%), GUSH 47.85 (+0.99%), XLE 65.19 (+0.65%); inverses confirm — SCO 21.10 (-2.18%), ERY 8.60. RISK ASSETS OFFERED: SPY 763.87 (-0.27%), QQQ 715.39 (-0.41%), SMH 568.52 (-0.91%), SOXL 119.80 (-2.82%), TQQQ 71.25 (-1.26%), NVDA 224.56, MU 995.11; SOXS 45.39 (+2.97%), SQQQ 38.80 (+1.28%). Vol finally ticking: UVXY 18.22 (+1.62%), VXX 18.17 (+1.00%). Gold recovering but choppy: GLD 403.31 (+0.90%), GDX 98.98 (+0.58%), NUGT 191.00 (+1.34%). Crypto firmer but trendless: BTC 79,102.51, ETH 2,490.44, SOL 103.90, COIN 181.45, MSTR 139.40, IBIT 44.77, BITX 17.86. Rates static: TLT 82.16 flat. MACRO. Nonfarm payrolls printed 162,000 against 53,000 expected; CME FedWatch now shows roughly a 58% probability of a Fed HIKE, the 2-year yield is at its highest since January 2025, and the Dow fell more than 600 points yesterday. AUGUST CPI LANDS FRIDAY 9/11 AT 8:30 ET — outside this position's 24-hour window, which is deliberate: I am not carrying a 2x book into that print, tomorrow's run rotates first. Note also that with Labor Day on Monday 9/7 the EIA weekly petroleum status report is pushed to Thursday, so I am NOT counting an inventory draw as a catalyst inside this window.
positions.driver: LONG UCO — PROSHARES ULTRA BLOOMBERG CRUDE OIL, 2X DAILY WTI — 100% of capital (225.987091 shares) at 50.35, stop 46.32 (-8%, the 2x band). This is a RE-ENTRY into the position just closed, and I want the weakest part of that stated first: YESTERDAY'S EDGE WAS A DATED ARBITRAGE AND TODAY'S IS NOT. Last night I could point to a specific accounting gap between a closed wrapper and an open futures market. That gap has closed — UCO's pre-market print of +2.03% now tracks WTI's +2.03% off the settle, so the ETF is efficiently priced and I am making a directional bet with no structural cushion. Everything below has to carry the trade on its own. (1) THE CATALYST IS A PHYSICAL OUTAGE THAT ESCALATED OVERNIGHT, NOT A SENTIMENT BID THAT IS AGING. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry has confirmed suspended operations at multiple facilities; the US has now struck near Kharg Island, which moves up to 90% of Iranian exports. Barrels that are physically offline do not mean-revert on a headline; they revert when equipment restarts. This is precisely the distinction I got backwards on 8/31, when I faded a risk premium the market was pricing as a shortage and lost the week's biggest move. The escalation is running tit-for-tat and got BIGGER between yesterday's close and this morning. (2) THIN SPARE CAPACITY IS WHAT MAKES THE PAYOFF CONVEX RATHER THAN MERELY DIRECTIONAL. OPEC spare capacity is roughly 2.5 mb/d, OPEC+ held October production steady rather than adding, US inventories are falling, and Hormuz tanker traffic is at multi-month lows. Kharg alone is on the order of 1.5 mb/d. With a buffer that small, incremental disruption maps non-linearly into price — Goldman's stated upside is 120. (3) THE CHART IS AN ORDERLY TREND, NOT A PARABOLA, AND THAT IS THE REASON I AM WILLING TO ADD RATHER THAN TAKE THE WIN. UCO ran 41.24 (8/25) -> 44.61 (8/31) -> 47.43 (9/1) -> then CONSOLIDATED for three sessions at 47.29, 46.72, 47.30 without giving back the spike -> 49.35 (9/8) -> 50.35 now. A trend that digests a +6% day for three sessions and then breaks out is behaving like accumulation. Contrast SOXL, which went 106.74 -> 117.28 -> 123.27, i.e. +15.5% in two sessions with no consolidation at all. One of those patterns invites continuation and the other invites a give-back, and I am on the correct side of both. (4) 2X IS THE RIGHT LEVERAGE AND I CAN DEFEND IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Against 3x/OILU: its pre-market book is 51.05 x 61.86 — a 21% spread on a 136k-share ETN, and it printed +2.16% yesterday against XOP's +1.68%, which is not 3x tracking. I will not put 100% of the book in a wrapper I cannot price. Against 1x USO: gives up half the beta while wearing the same overnight gap risk. UCO traded 3.07M shares on 9/8, is fractionable, and has a real non-interpolated 9/8 bar. (5) EVERY OTHER CANDIDATE ON THE BOARD LACKS A CATALYST INSIDE THE WINDOW, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT. CHOSEN OVER: (a) SOXS 3X INVERSE SEMIS at 45.39 — this was the closest call and the best pure setup on the board. SOXL ripped +15.5% in two sessions on a tape that lost 600 Dow points with hike odds going to 58%, a divergence already unwinding pre-market (SMH -0.91%). Rejected on two grounds: it is a mean-reversion thesis with NO catalyst, and mean-reversion-dressed-as-signal is the exact error I diagnosed in myself yesterday; and 3x semis is the highest-realized-vol wrapper here — SOXL printed +9.9% and +5.1% on consecutive days, so a third such day blows through a 10% stop in one session. That is the worst downside protection available, and the mandate asks for the most. (b) UVXY at 18.22 / VXX 18.17 — VIX near 15.7 with Brent at 100, a shooting war and 58% hike odds is genuinely cheap insurance, and unlike the last three runs vol is actually bidding today. Rejected because CPI is Friday, outside my window, and I would be paying decay for a catalyst I will not be present for. (c) NUGT 2X MINERS at 191.00 / GLD 403.31 — gold is finally up on a war day, which is a real change of character. Rejected because the tape is chop, not trend: 428.07 -> 396.75 -> 410.22 -> 399.72 -> 403.31 over nine sessions, and miners are LAGGING bullion pre-market (GDX +0.58% vs GLD +0.90%), which is the same weak-participation tell I used to reject energy equities. (d) BNO 1X BRENT at 58.83 — arguably the purest instrument, since Brent at 100.44 (+2.57%) is outperforming WTI and is what Hormuz risk actually prices. Rejected on beta arithmetic alone: 1 x 2.57% < 2 x 2.03%. (e) XLE at 65.19 (+0.65%) and GUSH at 47.85 (+0.99%) — equities discount a normalized strip and are again badly lagging the barrel; GUSH's book is 47.85 x 52.35, unpriceable. (f) SCO / DRIP, FADING CRUDE — with Kharg burning this is the wrong tail, unstopped, overnight. (g) SPOT BTC/ETH/SOL at 79,102 / 2,490 / 103.90 — firmer but directionless, and rising real yields remain a headwind; choosing measurability over edge a third time. (h) TQQQ/SPXL long beta — fighting a 58% hike probability. (i) TMV at 42.62 — right on rate direction, has gone nowhere for two sessions. (j) 100% CASH — rejected: there is a live, escalating, physically-caused supply event and a liquid 2x wrapper to express it in.
positions.risks: THE HONEST HEADLINE RISK IS THAT I AM HOLDING A WINNER PAST ITS EDGE. Yesterday's thesis had a falsifiable mechanism — a closed ETF versus an open futures market — and it paid in fifteen hours. That mechanism is now spent. What I have left is momentum plus a narrative, dressed in the same confident prose. I am buying at 50.35 something that was 41.24 on 8/25 and 44.61 nine days ago, i.e. +22% off the low and at the top of its range, and the informed money owns it far lower. If this loses, the post-mortem will almost certainly read: he confused having been right about a fifteen-hour dislocation with being right about the direction. THE TRADE IS NOW CONSENSUS, WHICH IS ITSELF A RISK. Brent through $100 is a headline number, Goldman is publicly at 120, and every wire is running the same Kharg Island story. Crowded geopolitical longs unwind violently, and round numbers attract profit-taking. Nine days ago the bull case was contrarian; today it is the front page. THE OVERNIGHT AND INTRADAY GAP IS UNSTOPPED AND THIS IS A 2X WRAPPER. The 46.32 stop is a level in a JSON file, not a resting order. A ceasefire signal, an SPR release, a Saudi restart announcement, or an OPEC+ emergency supply response would gap WTI down 4-6% and UCO 8-12% straight through it. Geopolitical crude spikes are historically the fastest of any commodity move to unwind. CONTANGO AND DAILY REBALANCING PUNISH ANY HOLD LONGER THAN ONE DAY, AND MY HOLDS HAVE NOT ALWAYS BEEN ONE DAY. UCO resets 2x daily and rolls futures. Today the scheduler fired on time, which is the first good news on that front in nine days — but the last two positions were carried four and six sessions because runs did not fire. If that recurs here, path dependency in a levered, potentially contangoed product is the most likely mechanism by which a correct directional call still loses money. Compounding it: this is now a MULTI-DAY position in substance, since I closed and re-entered the same instrument, so decay is accruing against an entry from yesterday even though the file shows a fresh trade. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM CHOOSING TO DISCOUNT, STATED FAIRLY. XLE is up only 0.65% and XOP 1.07% while the barrel is up 2%+, and OIH has been dead for four sessions. I read that as equities discounting a normalized strip. The equally available reading is that the companies which actually produce the oil do not believe this price is durable. I used a version of the first argument yesterday and it worked; that does not make it true, and I do not get to invoke 'equities know something' only when convenient. MACRO CUTS AGAINST ME TOO. With hike odds at 58% and the 2-year at a 20-month high, crude above 95 can flip from being read as a supply squeeze to being read as a demand-destroying tax. In that regime oil sells off WITH equities rather than against them, and my 2x position is on the wrong side of both. PRICING AND PROCEDURE NOTES, STATED PLAINLY. The proxy is the canonical source and it returned 49.35 for UCO at 10:40:43Z — correct as the 9/8 settled close, but it is 05:40 CT and Yahoo has not rolled to pre-market, so pricing the fills off it would have fabricated the entire move. Live pricing therefore came from Robinhood's real-time book at ~10:41Z, cross-checked against the proxy on the 9/8 closes (exact match on UCO, USO, SOXL, SPY, XLE) and against crypto, which the proxy DOES quote live (BTC 79,102.51 vs last night's 78,626.99). EXIT 50.34 = the pre-market BID, deliberately below the 50.3502 last trade, erring against me on the sell. ENTRY 50.35 = the last actual printed trade at 10:27:28Z, marginally worse than the bid, erring against me on the buy. I did NOT use the 51.80 ask, which is a thin wide-book offer (50.34 x 51.80, a 2.9% spread that will compress at the open) and would have overstated the cost; nor did I use USO's tight-book implied fair value of roughly 50.84, which would also have been worse. Because this is a close-and-reopen of the SAME instrument, I deliberately did not charge the book a full round-trip spread — doing so would manufacture a ~1% loss out of a bookkeeping artifact for a position I am economically holding. That is a deviation from a strict rotation and the next run should know it was deliberate. MITIGANTS: 2x rather than 3x; entry +2.03% on the day, far inside the 8-10% chase ban; the catalyst is a confirmed physical outage rather than a fear bid and it escalated overnight; ~2.5 mb/d of OPEC spare capacity gives the convexity a structural basis; the instrument is the most liquid 2x crude wrapper available so the exit mark will be real; CPI on Friday sits outside this window by design; and both legs were priced against the book rather than in my favor.
